title: Wave-Particle Duality and Quantum Observation
text:
Quantum mechanics mandates that fundamental particles exhibit both wave-like and particle-like properties. The precise manifestation of this duality is highly dependent on the experimental setup used for observation, a phenomenon demonstrated through the double-slit experiment.

The theory introduces complex concepts such as superposition, where a quantum system exists in multiple potential states simultaneously until measured. This leads directly to the measurement problem, which describes the transition from a probabilistic state to a single definite outcome upon interaction with a macroscopic measuring device.

Various interpretations attempt to resolve this inherent discontinuity—ranging from the collapse postulate of Copenhagen to the many-worlds interpretation—highlighting that observation itself plays an active role in defining physical reality.
